cards.explanation: The sound came "from heaven" (Acts 2:2). Not from the street, not from a neighbor's window. Then it filled the whole house where they were sitting, friends. I've heard a drawer slam shut over my head, but nothing like that.

The answer is True. They saw "…tongues like flames of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them." (Acts 2:3). Each of them, every single one. I stand next to an oven all day, friends, and I've never once had a flame show up and sit politely on my hat.

They were filled with the Holy Spirit. "…they were all filled with the Holy Spirit…" (Acts 2:4). All of them, not just a few. The Spirit is what filled them, plain and simple. And right after that, they began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.

The answer is language. "…each one heard them speaking his own language." (Acts 2:6). That's why the crowd came together in bewilderment, friends. Picture each person in that crowd hearing their own language.

The answer is Galilee. The crowd asks, "Are not all these who are speaking Galileans?" (Acts 2:7). Galileans, folks from the region of Galilee. They're asking how people from one place could be speaking so many languages. I wouldn't know either, friends, and I only speak Cookie.

The answer is God. The crowd says, "…we hear them declaring the wonders of God in our own tongues!" (Acts 2:11). So the topic wasn't small talk, friends. It was the wonders of God, and every listener heard it in their own tongue.

The answer is False. The crowd didn't get it right away. They were "Astounded and perplexed…" and they asked one another, "What does this mean?" (Acts 2:12). Hearing something amazing and understanding it are two different things, friends. I once stared at a mixer manual for a week, so I know that feeling.
The mockers said, "They are drunk on new wine!" (Acts 2:13). That was one reaction in the crowd, friends, because others were asking what it all meant. This story isn't finished, so stay with me.
